title: Certified Decisions
abstract: arXiv:2502.17830v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Hypothesis tests and confidence sets are ubiquitous in empirical research, yet their connection to subsequent decision-making is often unclear. We view statistical inference as pairing recommended decisions with guarantees of their quality---or certificates---and develop a theory of certified decisions. Specifically, we attach P-certificates---upper bounds on loss that hold with probability at least $1-\alpha$---to recommended actions. We prove that it is without loss to limit attention to P-certificates generated by minimax decisions over confidence sets, or what Manski (2021) terms "as-if decisions with a set estimate." We further show that such certificates allow safe adoption decisions for ambiguity-averse downstream decision-makers. A parallel argument applies to E-certified decisions obtained from e-values in settings with unbounded loss. We illustrate this view of statistical inference through an application to economic mobili

translated_abstract: 假设检验和置信集在实证研究中无处不在，但它们与后续决策之间的联系往往不清晰。我们将统计推断视为把推荐决策与其质量保证（即“证书”）相配对，并据此发展了一套认证决策理论。具体而言，我们为推荐行动附加P证书——即以至少 $1-\alpha$ 的概率成立的损失上界。我们证明，将注意力局限于由置信集上的极小极大决策所生成的P证书（即 Manski (2021) 所称的“基于集合估计的仿佛式决策”）是不失一般性的。我们进一步表明，此类证书能使对模糊性厌恶的下游决策者做出安全的采纳决策。类似的论证也适用于在损失无界的设定下由 e 值获得的 E 认证决策。我们通过对经济流动性的应用来阐释这一统计推断视角。
tldr: 该论文提出“认证决策”理论，将统计推断理解为为推荐决策附加以至少1-α概率成立的损失上界证书，并证明只需关注由置信集上的极小极大决策生成的证书即可，这使模糊厌恶的下游决策者能够安全地采纳统计建议。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a theory of certified decisions—pairing recommended actions with loss upper bounds that hold with probability at least 1-α—and proves it is without loss to focus on certificates generated by minimax decisions over confidence sets, enabling safe adoption decisions for ambiguity-averse downstream decision-makers.
